study.title: Effects of organic acids on the edema of the stria vascularis induced by furosemide

protocol.pretreatment_note: The abstract states the 30-minute delay for both saline controls and experimental pretreatments.
protocol.recovery_definition: Time from drug injection until recovery of EP to 80% of control.
recovery_caveats: The timing of EP measurement versus tissue collection at 10, 20 and 30 minutes is not reconciled for each animal.
The paper does not specify the exact rule for trajectories that never fall below 80% of control, multiple crossings, or incomplete recovery.
The table gives group means of individual endpoints, not endpoints of a group-average trajectory.

table_i.significance: Against saline control, all EP reductions P < 0.01; penicillin recovery time P < 0.05.
table_i.limitations: The covariance of EP drop and recovery is not reported; uncertainties for each endpoint are not independent animal observations. The relation between these groups and tissue specimens needs clarification.

morphology.method: electron microscopy of basal-turn lateral wall
morphology.rater_blinding: Two individuals ranked coded photomicrographs without knowing treatment.

saline_control_text_observations.source: PDF page 3, prose; data not shown

morphology.temporal_comparison: The authors describe more edema at 10 than 20 minutes, with clearance at 30 minutes. The representative EP minimum occurs within two to three minutes; 10 minutes is the worst of the shown later tissue samples, not a proven continuous-time peak.
morphology.sampling_caveat: The 3-minute samples are mentioned in prose but absent from the Figure 1 bars. The animal count per tissue time, overlap with EP animals, and aggregation or inter-rater agreement for the plotted bars are not established.
morphology.limitations: Ordinal photomicrograph ratings are not continuous fluid volume or water flux; inter-rater agreement and animal-level mapping were not extracted.
